Synopsis:
Three people are having an argument. Rolan, Lia and Cal. Lia and Cal are brother and sister, but the three of them have grown up together. They're young, talented tieflings who are heading to Baldur's Gate to start their lives and careers. Rolan argues that they should leave now and get to the city while they still can. Lia argues that it is irresponsible to leave their kin behind. Cal is stuck in the middle.
This is a passionate and fiery argument, both sides are convinced that they are correct.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_Prodigy_Group.json: Rolan, Lia and Cal are young tieflings who grew up together; Lia and Cal are siblings and the three are debating whether to leave for Baldur’s Gate or stay to help their people. Off‑screen they’re amid the tense aftermath of a goblin attack: tiefling refugees are sheltering in the Emerald Grove, druids and leaders (and possibly Halsin or Kagha) have been involved in recent violence, and the camp is raw and uncertain. That recent fighting, druid distrust of tieflings, and talk of sealing the grove have made the choice urgent—some see escape as survival, others see staying as a duty to kin. Cal stands between two passionate, convinced positions, trying to calm a fight that’s as much about safety as it is about identity.
- DEN_Prodigy.json: This short exchange takes place immediately after a heated argument with Lia, during the Emerald Grove’s tense post‑battle aftermath—the party has already been through the goblin fight and Kagha was saved and is present. Private scenes (for example, with Kagha’s parents) have happened off‑screen, so wounds, fear, and talk of Halsin or the wolf pens color the camp’s mood. Rolan’s lines show the split outcome: if the party is leaving for Baldur’s Gate he’s breezy and dismissive of Lia’s anger; if they stay he’s furious and convinced the grove will get them killed.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Reunion.json: Cal and/or Lia have been rescued from Moonrise towers and reunited with Rolan in Last Light Inn. It is initially a tense scene - Rolan was worried sick/is angry one of his siblings is dead and is taking it out on his family. It is up to the player to calm them down and remind them of what is important - family.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_AD_BeforeReunion.json: This AD covers the following scenarios: Lia alive, Cal dead. Cal alive, Lia dead. Cal, Lia and Rolan all alive and well. This AD occurs after the player has rescued Cal and/ or Lia from Moonrise towers, but BEFORE the player triggers the reunion scene in Last Light. The siblings are standing together and arguing.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Brother.json: Cal has been rescued from Moonrise Towers by the player and is now in Last Light. This dialogue covers multiple states: Rolan is missing, Rolan is dead, Rolan and Cal had a fight (player must pass a persuade to calm the fight, pass and fail states here), and a general state for when cal, lia and rolan are all alive and well and cal is grateful to the player.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Lia: Hells, we can't just leave. They're kin. || [context] NodeContext: This is the start of the dialog but clearly an ongoing argument. You think it's your responsibility, as a tiefling, to stay and help your kin. You're angry, voice is level but will soon grow louder, and utterly convinced that staying at the camp is the right thing to do. (node 3)
- Rolan: I'll not gamble our lives, our futures, on people who are as good as dead. We must leave for Baldur's Gate - at once. || [context] NodeContext: You're angry but your voice is level. You think staying at the camp is essentially suicide. You cannot believe it was even suggested. You and your friends have brand new lives waiting for you in Baldur's Gate - to stay at the camp is reckless and pointless to you. (node 45)
- Cal: Can we all just take a moment? Please? || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Looking for one to the other. Stuck in between them, pleading. Hands out as he tries to calm the situation. NodeContext: Your friend and sister are screaming at each other in front of you. Light and easygoing tone as you try to calm the argument. (node 10)
- Lia: What's the point in blades and spells if we don't bloody use them? We should stay. || [context] NodeContext: Your voice is getting louder. You're very angry now. It's your civic duty to use the skills you have to help people. You cannot believe how selfish Rolan is being. (node 47)
- Lia: These people aren't fighters. We can help. || [context] NodeContext: Ibid. (node 21)
- Cal: Or yell louder. That's fine too. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Sighing as he shrugs. He knows neither is listening to him. NodeContext: Your friend and sister have ignored your plea. You know once they've started they'll just keep arguing until one of them gives in. This is almost said with a shrug and in a light, jokey tone. (node 43)

context: Rolan, Lia and Cal are three young tieflings who grew up together; Lia and Cal are siblings and the trio are supposed to be heading to Baldur’s Gate to begin new lives. The scene takes place in the tense aftermath of a goblin attack at the Emerald Grove: tiefling refugees are sheltering there, druids and leaders (and possibly Halsin or Kagha) have been involved in recent violence, and talk of sealing the grove has made the choice urgent. Rolan argues they must leave now to save their futures, while Lia insists it would be irresponsible—indeed a moral duty—to stay and help their kin. Cal is stuck between the two, trying to calm a passionate fight that’s as much about survival as identity.
